subject: history
title: Roman Britain to the Norman Conquest
welcome_lead: Trace Britain from Roman province to Norman kingdom across a millennium of upheaval.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on Roman Britain, the Anglo-Saxons and the Norman Conquest of 1066.
final_note: You have crossed from Hadrian's Wall to the Battle of Hastings.

concepts.def: Britain as a Roman province from AD 43 (Claudian invasion) until c. AD 410, leaving roads, towns and Christianity.
Germanic peoples (Angles, Saxons, Jutes) who settled Britain after c. 450, forming kingdoms such as Wessex and Mercia.
Anglo-Saxon council of nobles and clergy that advised the king and could confirm royal succession.
William of Normandy's invasion of England in 1066, culminating in the Battle of Hastings on 14 October 1066.
Hierarchical landholding system in which the king granted fiefs to tenants-in-chief in return for military service.
1086 survey of land and resources commissioned by William I to assess tax and consolidate Norman rule.

walkthroughs.h2: Why did Harold lose at Hastings?
walkthroughs.body_html: Harold Godwinson was crowned in January 1066 but faced two invasions. He defeated Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge on 25 September, then force-marched south. At Hastings on 14 October, exhausted housecarls held the ridge until feigned Norman retreats broke the shield wall. William's combined cavalry, archers and infantry proved decisive, and Harold's death ended Anglo-Saxon resistance.

William replaced almost the entire Anglo-Saxon aristocracy with Norman tenants-in-chief, built motte-and-bailey castles to dominate the landscape, and reorganised the Church under Lanfranc. The 1086 Domesday Book recorded every manor for taxation. Latin and Norman French replaced Old English in elite use, embedding a continental feudal order.

King John's military failures in France and heavy taxation provoked baronial revolt. At Runnymede in June 1215 he sealed Magna Carta, limiting arbitrary royal power and asserting that free men could not be imprisoned without lawful judgement. Though immediately annulled by the Pope, it was reissued and became a touchstone of constitutional liberty.
